memo.verdict: PARK at Triaging, high conviction. Do not progress to Early-Stage Assessment on current evidence. Retain on the Triaging watchlist at a quarterly review cadence, not the monthly cadence reserved for names with a live entry thesis. Re-run after the Q3 2026 print in early November 2026 and after the EUR 300m rights-issue outcome is known. The memo adopts in full the Risks report's own section 14 recommendation to defer any active long position until the strategic reset translates into actual cash flow expansion. Two named conditions would flip the answer: average fibre selling prices and sales volumes rising together for two consecutive quarters with clean earnings, and Chinese generic lyocell operating rates plus announced capacity stabilising. Named immediate re-run triggers carried from the Risks report: generic viscose staple fibre prices falling below CNY 12,000 per tonne, and severance spending exceeding the EUR 40m provision.
case: The case for parking runs in five steps, and the memo builds it in that order.

Step one: the change forces are real but one-sided. Internal change is the strongest single feature of the case and graded [B] at Element E1 RA1 CQ2. The performance programme delivered over EUR 200m of cost savings in FY25 against EUR 130m in FY24, with the recurring annual target raised from EUR 100m to EUR 180m. About 600 Austrian administrative roles are being cut by late 2027, over 200 legally terminated by Q1 2026 delivering EUR 25m, with annual savings of over EUR 45m expected by 2027 and around 300 roles relocated to North America and Asia. Heiligenkreuz closes by end-2026 and Grimsby by end-2027, carrying up to EUR 150m of non-cash impairments and EUR 40m of provisions in 2026. The 55.2% TreeToTextile majority cost EUR 24.18m and produced a EUR 12m badwill gain. External change forces, by contrast, grade [D]: global clothing markets grew only 1.0% to 2.0% in 2025, and the one genuine tailwind, lyocell demand projected to grow in excess of 20% annually, is out-competed by supply, since global generic lyocell capacity has more than doubled over three years.

Step two: the base those forces act on fails, and grades [F] at Element E1 RA2. Consolidated net losses in every fiscal year from 2022 through 2025. Return on capital employed of 0.70%. Adjusted equity ratio down 510 basis points to 29.6%. Net leverage of 3.30 times sitting 80 basis points above Suzano's sub-2.50-times threshold, with a 130-basis-point annual deleveraging pace implying two more years to reach it. The one leg that passes is that the base is well invested: capex down to EUR 141m from an EUR 844m 2021 peak, Brazil and Thailand complete, EUR 200m of upgrades converting 100% of fibre sites to specialty production, and a 14 megawatt power-to-heat facility commissioned in April 2026. Delivery congruency grades [D] because the three consecutive qualitative guidance beats lean on one-off items: EUR 45.1m of carbon allowance sales in FY25, more than 15% of FY25 reported EBITDA from non-recurring gains, and EUR 39m of one-offs at 33.62% of Q1 2026 reported EBITDA.
counter_case: The memo carries three counter-arguments and does not soften them.

First, the source's own sell-side-groupthink counter, preserved verbatim from the change-forces report: sell-side groupthink may be excessively discounting Lenzing's restructuring self-help, and if the roughly EUR 200m annual cost savings programme runs fully to plan, deleveraging will occur much faster than current consensus models suggest, triggering rapid rating upgrades. The memo rejects it on the ground that the savings are already largely inside the FY25 numbers, and the fibre division still earned only EUR 0.10m with them banked. That rejection is contestable: it assumes the FY25 savings are fully run-rated, and the source separately says a further over EUR 45m per annum arrives by 2027.
triggers: What would change the view, in the memo's own terms.

Reassessment criteria, all eight as stated. One: fibre division earnings above EUR 100m for two consecutive quarters with average selling prices and volumes rising together rather than volume alone. Two: net debt to earnings below 2.50 times on a post-rights-issue basis with the 9.00% hybrid refinanced or redeemed. Three: reported earnings above EUR 400m clean of one-off items, excluding carbon allowance sales, badwill and joint-venture consolidation effects. Four: Heiligenkreuz closed by end-2026 inside the EUR 40m provision and Grimsby wound down by end-2027. Five: Chinese generic lyocell operating rates and announced capacity stabilising, with no further plant of Sateri's scale entering construction. Six: generic viscose staple fibre pricing in China sustained above RMB 13,500 a tonne, against RMB 13,280 in Q1 2026. Seven: immediate re-run trigger if generic viscose prices fall below CNY 12,000 a tonne. Eight: immediate re-run trigger if severance spending exceeds the EUR 40m provision.

Next-stage questions the memo would carry into an Early-Stage Assessment. How much of the EUR 550m 2027 earnings ambition is cost-out and how much needs fibre price recovery the supply curve will not allow. What is the post-rights-issue net leverage and hybrid refinancing path, and does it reach below 2.50 times without a further raise. What are the actual Chinese generic lyocell operating rates and net capacity additions, which the Risks report names as its own priority data gap. Does the EUR 327.6m Dexco put option crystallise, and on what trigger, given it equals 24% of market capitalisation. Can average fibre selling prices and volumes rise together for two consecutive quarters, the single test that separates recovery from false friend.

Monitoring lines opened. Monthly: Western European caustic soda spot prices, which the Risks report calls a leading indicator for multiple operational failures, and Chinese generic lyocell operating rates. Quarterly: realised cost savings against the EUR 45m 2027 target, with a warning threshold below EUR 20m per annum; and the spread between average fibre selling prices and sales volumes, which the Risks report names the definitive early-warning indicator.

Named calendar events. The extraordinary general meeting on the EUR 300m capital increase in August 2026, which the Risks report calls the first hurdle. The Q3 2026 print in early November 2026. Heiligenkreuz closure by end-2026. Grimsby phase-out by end-2027.

Data gaps recorded rather than filled. No leadership-foundations report exists on disk for this ticker, checked directly; every governance judgement is drawn from the change-forces and business-foundations digests. No 52-week range in the supplied dashboard data. No usable forward multiple. No consensus rating mix, with a research pool of one covering analyst. Five of six peers have no master digest, so peer anchors are ratings-only cold-start anchors. The assembled coverage report wrongly states "Above-floor reports present: none" while business-foundations and risks are both on disk; the folder was checked directly and both were read, and the coverage line is flagged as a pipeline defect.

defs.atr: average true range: each day's high to low, stretched to the previous close on a gap, as a % of the previous close; L5D the last 5 sessions, L1M and L3M the last 30 and 91 calendar days
defs.top_half: a close above the midpoint of the day's high-low range; an up day closes at or above the previous close; days with no range are left out
